title: Leaf Punch DNA Extraction
author: Alex Rajewski
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yxufxnw
materials: Make a 0.5M EDTA solution by dissolving 93.05g of EDTA in ~400mL of DI water. Adjust the pH to 8 by adding ~20g of NaOH. Bring to 500mL and autoclave. Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid disodium salt dihydrate Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #E4884 undetermined, EDTA undetermined, NaOH undetermined, DI water The disodium salt of EDTA will not dissolve until the pH is near 8.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary stock solutions and buffers for the extraction.

substeps.instruction: Make 1M Tris solution: dissolve 78.8g Tris-HCl in 500mL DI water, adjust pH to 8 with HCl, and autoclave.
Make 5M NaCl solution: dissolve 146g NaCl in ~400mL DI water, bring to 500mL, and autoclave.
Make 10% SDS solution: dissolve 50g sodium dodecyl sulphate in ~400mL DI water, heat to 65ºC to dissolve, and bring to 500mL.
Prepare Edward's Buffer: combine 1M Tris (pH 8), 5M NaCl, 0.5M EDTA, and 10% SDS, bring to 1L with DI water, and autoclave.

steps.title: Collect and Store Leaf Tissue
steps.instruction: Collect young leaf tissue and store it at ultra-low temperature.

substeps.instruction: Collect a young leaf (the size of a penny) into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Store tubes at -80°C until extraction.

steps.title: Grind Leaf Tissue
steps.instruction: Mechanically disrupt the frozen tissue into a fine powder using liquid nitrogen.

substeps.instruction: Snap freeze tubes in a dewar of liquid nitrogen (LN2).
Freeze a plastic tube rack by pouring LN2 into it until it no longer evaporates.
Remove a tube from the dewar, warm the hinge with fingers to prevent breaking, and place it in an LN2-containing well (ensure no LN2 enters the tube).
Grind tissue to a fine powder using a plastic pestle, transferring the tube to a new well every ~10 seconds to prevent thawing.
Close the tube and return it to the dewar.

steps.title: Lysis and Incubation
steps.instruction: Extract DNA using the Edwards buffer and NaCl mixture.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a mixture of 750µL 60% Edwards buffer and 40% 5M NaCl for each tube.
Add 750µL of this Edwards/NaCl mixture to each tube and vortex.
Incubate at 60ºC for 30 minutes, inverting 2-3 times during incubation to mix.
Optional: Allow tubes to sit at -20ºC for at least 15 minutes (or overnight).

steps.title: Initial Centrifugation and Precipitation
steps.instruction: Separate the supernatant and precipitate the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 5 minutes at 13,000 rpm.
While spinning, add 1mL of 100% ethanol into a new, clearly labeled tube.
Transfer 500µL of the supernatant into the ethanol tube without disturbing the pellet.
Gently invert the ethanol tube several times to mix until a white-ish, wispy cloud (DNA precipitate) appears.

steps.title: DNA Pellet Recovery
steps.instruction: Wash and isolate the DNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the ethanol tubes for 5 minutes at 13,000 rpm.
Add 300µL of 70% ethanol and centrifuge for 5 minutes at 13,000 rpm (do not resuspend the pellet).
Carefully pour off the ethanol, turn the tube upside down for no more than 2 seconds, and blot with paper towels.

steps.title: Ethanol Evaporation
steps.instruction: Remove all remaining ethanol from the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Allow the plate to sit for ~10 minutes at 60ºC to evaporate ethanol.
Verify ethanol evaporation by visual inspection or wafting; no ethanol should be seen or smelled.

steps.title: DNA Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final DNA pellet in buffer.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 200 µl of 1x TE buffer (or water).
Rotate the plate upside down gently several times to mix.
Optional: Place tubes on a shaker at 200rpm for ~30 minutes to resuspend.
